papers.title: Sets of reach $R$ are $\operatorname{CAT}\left( 1/R^2\right)$
papers.abstract: Positive reach underpins many results in computational geometry and topology. It is used for triangulation criteria, topological inference, and manifold learning. The geometric properties of these sets have therefore been studied intensely. In this paper we focus on the intrinsic metric properties of sets of positive reach. In particular we give an elementary proof of the fact that (closed) sets of reach at least $R$ are $\operatorname{CAT}(1/R^2)$. This fact was established earlier by Alexander and Bishop, using quite significant machinery. The fact that a space is $\operatorname{CAT}(1/R^2)$ offers many advantages, such as the uniqueness and continuity of sufficiently short geodesics, the existence of Fr{\'e}chet means and by extension the Rips based homotopy reconstruction of Hausmann is available.

papers.title: Minimum central circles: an effective characterization of the global asymptotic constant
papers.abstract: Let $R^\ast(n)$ be the minimum radius of a central circle externally tangent to nonoverlapping circles of radii $1,\ldots,n$. We prove that $R^\ast(n)=C_\ast n^2+o(n^2)$ and give finite linear programs that enclose $C_\ast$ with prescribed error. An exact angular comparison reduces the problem to marked points on a line with separation at least the geometric mean of each pair of marks. Concatenation with bounded joining cost and reassignment to the prescribed normalized radii prove existence of the limit. Balanced finite-word programs give a bracket of width $(1/k+1/r)/\pi$, before directed arithmetic error, using $k$ types and words of length $r$. We also obtain explicit geometric bounds. For the upper bound, we recover finite and countable reflected-block constructions by actual permutations, retaining all pair constraints. A coupled terminal-subset argument gives an explicit lower bound strictly above $1/8$. Together these give $C_{\rm term}+\eta_{\rm width}\le C_\ast\le U_4$. The lower endpoint comes from the terminal-subset argument, and the upper endpoint from the four-block construction; neither is asserted sharp. The finite-word scheme establishes computability; efficient high-precision evaluation and the structure of global optimizers remain open.

papers.title: Confronting Uncertainty in Mechanism-AI Coupled Dynamical Systems via Optimal Transport and Information Geometry: Part I. Distribution Learning
papers.abstract: Mechanism-AI coupled dynamical systems are increasingly used to study complex biological systems. However, uncertainty associated with noisy, sparse, and partially observed data limits their reliability. This paper presents a systematic mathematical formulation for treating these uncertainties from the perspective of optimal transport and information geometry. We formulate the uncertainty quantification problem as the minimization of an energy functional on a probability density space equipped with a Riemannian metric, with the loss evaluated through a differential equation, and give a unified description of the gradient flows of the energy functional under specific metrics, such as the Wasserstein and Fisher-Rao metrics. Furthermore, we present corresponding numerical methods for solving these gradient flows using abstract adjoint sensitivity analysis. The formulation connects a range of Bayesian inference methods for dynamical systems; numerical experiments compare posterior approximation and predictive uncertainty under a common computational budget. Moreover, it also provides a geometric perspective on dynamical modeling and the study of heterogeneity evolution.

papers.title: A reverse entropy power inequality for i.i.d. log-concave random variables
papers.abstract: We show that $h_\infty(X+Y)\leq h_\infty(Z+W)$, where $X, Y$ are independent log-concave random variables, and $Z, W$ are exponential random variables having the same respective $\infty$-R\'enyi entropies. Analogs for integer-valued monotone log-concave random variables are also obtained. Our main tools are decreasing rearrangement, majorization, and the change of measure.

papers.title: The Whitney Extension Problem in Carnot groups
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb{G}$ be a Carnot group, let $E \subset \mathbb{G}$ be compact, and suppose we are given a function $f: E \to \mathbb{R}$. The $C^1_H$ {\em Whitney Extension Problem} asks the following: what must be true about $f$ to guarantee that there exists a smooth, horizontal function $F \in C^1_H(\mathbb{G})$ extending $f$, i.e., there is some $F:\mathbb{G} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that $F|_E = f|_E$ and $XF$ is continuous for every horizontal left invariant vector field $X$? We adapt the method of G. Glaeser and C. Fefferman to answer this question in this non-commutative setting. Moreover, we provide an alternative solution to the $C^1$ Whitney Extension Problem for horizontal curves in the Heisenberg group.

papers.title: Bounded ratios for Lorentzian matrices
papers.abstract: We study multiplicative inequalities among entries of Lorentzian matrices, referred to as bounded ratios. These inequalities can be viewed as generalizations of the classical Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities for mixed volumes. Our main structural result identifies the cone of all bounded ratios on Lorentzian matrices with the dual of the cut cone, a finitely generated integral polyhedral cone extensively studied in metric geometry and graph theory. We examine in detail the pentagonal ratio, which first appears for Lorentzian matrices of size at least five. For Lorentzian matrices of size three, we determine the optimal bounding constants across the entire cone of bounded ratios, obtaining an explicit entropy-like formula.

papers.title: On maximum volume polytopes inscribed in the sphere
papers.abstract: We combine degree sequence bounds with a supporting tangent plane method to study maximum volume polytopes inscribed in the sphere $\mathbb S^2$. Building on the vertex-star estimates and combinatorial reductions in Wimmer's dissertation, we determine the exact maximum for ten vertices and the unique maximizing combinatorial type for eleven vertices. Moreover, using explicit computational certificates we identify a unique possible maximizing type for polytopes with thirteen and fifteen vertices, and two possible types for sixteen vertices; this approach also recovers Wimmer's fourteen-vertex combinatorial theorem. Finally, we derive a facial inequality which holds for every degree pattern, and prove that the maximum volume for polytopes with thirty-two vertices is $\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{10(5-\sqrt{5})}$, attained precisely by an inscribed realization of the pentakis dodecahedron, which is the convex hull of the regular icosahedron together with its normalized facet centers. Wimmer had already determined this configuration and its optimality within its own combinatorial type. We also obtain a global degree sequence envelope and a universal affine volume bound.

papers.title: Controlled Riemannian rigidity
papers.abstract: Given a compact Lie group acting smoothly and freely on a compact connected manifold, we prove that the space of invariant Riemannian metrics whose symmetry group is precisely the group in question is open dense in that of all invariant metrics provided the orbit space is sufficiently large. This strengthens the author's prior results and recovers Ebin's to the effect that trivial-symmetry Riemannian metrics constitute an open dense set. In the process, the discussion also addresses a number of apparent gaps in said sources, pertaining to the rigidity results in question.

papers.title: Cube tilings, partition counters, and the Calkin--Wilf and Kepler trees
papers.abstract: A tiling of the integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ by translates of the discrete cube $K_d=\{0,1\}^d$ cuts every translate $K_d+x$ into subcubes. We study the function $\ell(x)$ counting these parts. Its sum over every translate of $K_d$ equals $3^d$, for an arbitrary translation set. For lattice tilings with a triangular basis we obtain a dimension-reduction formula, and we describe every cocyclic lattice by a single normalized congruence. Along a cyclic generator, the counter of a signed bidiagonal lattice is a row of Stern's diatomic sequence; pairs of counter values realize the Calkin--Wilf tree, and complementary binary words realize the Kepler tree. For the binary lattice, the translated counter labelings of the cube carry generating face partitions, supplied by the tiling itself, which force the levels of the Kepler tree, and every nontrivial face partition has a unique lamination direction. Using finite Fourier analysis we prove that the ordered cyclic profile determines a standard cocyclic cube tiling lattice up to coordinate reflections. For lattices tiling by discrete boxes we determine exactly when the analogous statement holds.

papers.title: Odd realisation numbers of rigid graphs
papers.abstract: Determining the number of realisations of a rigid graph for a specific choice of edge lengths is a fundamental problem in discrete geometry. Gortler, Healy and Thurston showed that the number of real realisations of a generic framework is always even or equal to one. Despite being rare, there do exist graphs whose number of complex realisations is odd and not equal to one. In this article, we exhibit two necessary conditions for a rigid graph to have an odd realisation number other than one. We also provide an infinite family of rigid graphs with an odd realisation number other than one.

papers.title: The inscribed $4$-polytope of maximal volume with nine vertices
papers.abstract: We prove that a $4$-polytope with nine vertices inscribed in the unit sphere $\mathbb{S}^{3}$ has volume at most $\frac{5}{24}\sqrt{10 + 2\sqrt{5}}$, and that, up to orthogonal transformations, equality holds only for the convex hull of a square and a regular pentagon inscribed in $\mathbb{S}^{3}$ in orthogonal $2$-planes through the origin. For the combinatorial type of this polytope, whose boundary complex is the join of a $4$-cycle and a $5$-cycle, we write the signed volume as the pairing, through the Hodge star, of the area vectors of the two cycles, and bound each area vector by finite Fourier analysis; the bound holds for every choice of nine points on the sphere. Since an optimal polytope is simplicial, by a result of Horv\'ath and L\'angi, it remains to exclude the other simplicial types, which we do by sum-of-squares certificates checked in exact arithmetic.

papers.title: Optimal rational spherical designs on the circle
papers.abstract: The minimum numbers of points in rational equal-weight spherical designs on the circle are $2304$, $4608$, $9216$, and $9216$ at strengths $4$, $5$, $6$, and $7$, respectively. We construct two nonisometric optimal designs at each strength. At arbitrary strength $t$, we obtain an explicit cardinality divisor $D_t$ with $\log D_t=(1/2+o(1))t\log t$. Applied to the antipodal pairs of a $4608$-point design, Gromov's torus construction gives a flat minimal immersion of $\mathbb{T}^2$ into $S^{4607}$ with $2304$ distinct integral frequencies, attaining Petrunin's sharp Euclidean normal-curvature bound.

papers.title: Compact metric spaces as exponentiable metric compact Hausdorff spaces
papers.abstract: The class of compact metric spaces (metric spaces which induce a compact topology), despite being an important class of metric spaces, is not closed under many natural constructions. For instance, infinite metric products of compact metric spaces will often fail to induce a compact topology, while on the other hand, the topological product of any family of compact metric spaces is always a compact topological space, evidencing a discrepancy between topological and metric products. The notion of metric compact Hausdorff space -- compact Hausdorff spaces equipped with a lower semi-continuous metric -- provides a class of spaces which keep track of metric data and topological data separately, thereby forming a complete and cocomplete category, while including all compact metric spaces. Our main contribution is that this inclusion can be characterised via universal property: the compact metric spaces are the exponentiable metric compact Hausdorff spaces with respect to a natural monoidal structure on the respective category.

papers.title: Fractal solutions to the two-dimensional floating body problem
papers.abstract: In this paper, the first construction of an entire class of two-dimensional fractal bodies that float in water in equilibrium is explicitly given. Their boundaries are described by planar fractal Zindler curves which are constructed using fractal projective hedgehogs. The areas of these bodies are seen to be well-defined and their expression is explicitly computed. To this end, a result concerning the continuity of the Lebesgue measure with respect to the Hausdorff metric for compact sets is given. Furthermore, the Hausdorff dimension $w$ of these fractal curves is shown to coincide with the Hausdorff dimension of the graph of a Weierstrass function associated to the corresponding fractal projective hedgehog. The fractal Zindler curves are proved to have halving chords of constant length that split both the area and the $w$-dimensional Hausdorff measure of the curve into exact halves.

papers.title: Coarse Embeddings Beyond Doubling: Persistence Diagrams and Multiparameter Modules
papers.abstract: We study coarse embeddings into Hilbert space and the asymptotic dimension of spaces of persistence diagrams and multiparameter persistence modules. We replace doubling, the usual hypothesis for landmark embeddings, by admissible tent covers of bounded multiplicity at every scale: stacking them across dyadic scales gives an explicit $1$-Lipschitz coarse embedding, with lower gauge $c\sqrt{\tau t}$, or nearly linear for slowly decaying weights, and the same covers bound the asymptotic dimension by the multiplicity. The spaces of persistence diagrams are not doubling but carry such covers, and for diagrams with $n$ points our covers improve the constant of the known landmark embedding by a factor exponential in $n$. Slice by slice, the construction embeds multiparameter modules with boundedly many bars per slice under the matching distance on any finite net of slices, a class that contains the modules with at most $n$ generators. Bounding bars or persistent Betti numbers instead of generators fails: two-parameter modules with one bar on every slice have infinite asymptotic dimension, and neither they nor the modules of bounded support and bounded rank admit a coarse embedding into Hilbert space, under the matching or the interleaving distance.

papers.title: Two-mode stability for multi-marginal optimal transport maps
papers.abstract: We establish a two-mode stability theory for Monge solutions of the multi-marginal optimal transport problem with barycentric quadratic cost. The associated tuple of maps splits into an external barycentric mode and internal relative modes. A quadratic lower bound for the Kantorovich defect controls the internal modes and yields a square-root estimate without invoking any two-marginal map-stability theorem. The external mode is the optimal transport map from the fixed source to the Wasserstein barycenter. Combining the resulting two-mode estimate with M\'erigot's sharp theorem gives a $\frac{1}{4}$-H\"older estimate for general perturbations, while barycenter-preserving perturbations satisfy a $\frac{1}{2}$-H\"older estimate. We prove that both exponents and the dependence on the weights are optimal. We also examine the scope of such decomposition beyond the barycentric cost: collective-coordinate perturbations and uniformly concave costs of the sum retain the two-mode estimate, whereas the analyses of graph interactions, hedonic costs, and translation-invariant costs identify the two possible obstructions -- loss of relative coercivity and lack of stability for the remaining external modes.

papers.title: The Zaporozhets-Tarasov Conjecture on Mean Distances
papers.abstract: For a convex body $K \subset \mathbb R^d$ let $\Delta(K)$ be the expected distance between two independent uniform points of $K$, and let $\theta(K)$ be the corresponding expectation for normalized surface measure on $\partial K$. The Zaporozhets-Tarasov conjecture asserts $\Delta(K) \le \theta(K)$. We prove this conjecture in case $d=2$. In addition, we give a six-vertex convex polytope in $\mathbb R^3$ for which the reverse strict inequality holds, and obtain counterexamples in every dimension $d \ge 3$ by taking products with segments.

papers.title: A Dimension-Free Bound on the Poincar\'e Constant of Isotropic Log-Concave Measures
papers.abstract: The Kannan--Lov\'asz--Simonovits (KLS) conjecture asserts that isotropic log-concave probability measures have Poincar\'e constants bounded by a universal constant, independently of dimension. In this work, we provide a deterministic variational proof that the Poincar\'e constant $C_P(\mu)\le25$, where $\mu$ is any isotropic log-concave probability measure. The proof centers on mean-zero integration of compatible symmetric tensor fields. Starting from constant tensors, we obtain factorially normalized Appell polynomials by iterating this procedure. Using moment estimates and a quadratic variance inequality, we establish geometric bounds on these iterated primitives through a \emph{joint} variational argument over the measure and test function. At a maximizing pair, stationarity in the test function controls the weighted sum of the two highest-order cumulant terms arising from the measure variation. To extend these bounds to arbitrary compatible fields, we use a weighted Helmholtz--Hodge decomposition of weighted divergence, the formal adjoint of differentiation. Controlling the curl in the decomposition yields a curvature comparison for the integration operators, uniformly in tensor order. Combining this comparison with the Appell bounds gives a bound on the full integration operator and hence the stated Poincar\'e inequality. The estimate is independent of the auxiliary positive curvature, allowing approximation to general isotropic log-concave measures.

papers.title: Euclidean view-obstruction in dimensions eight to ten and the asymptotic deficit
papers.abstract: The Euclidean view-obstruction problem asks for the critical radius of balls centered at the half-integer lattice that meet every positive ray from the origin. Writing $\Delta_n$ for its square, we determine $\Delta_8=8/17$, $\Delta_9=1087/1980$ and $\Delta_{10}=7/11$ by computer-assisted proofs using Kahlon's seven-dimensional theorem.The upper bounds combine full-support subspace averaging, projected lattice coverings and exact finite certificates; dimension ten also requires a finite search through short integer relations. Explicit directions attain all three values, including a ten-dimensional direction previously listed by Gritsenko, Skoruppa and Zagier. In arbitrary dimension, we express their theta-block invariant in geometric normalization and derive the known bounds $c\log(n+1) \le n/12 - \Delta_n \le C\log^3(n+1)$, with repeated coordinates allowed throughout. Thus $\Delta_n \sim n/12$, while the deficit tends to infinity more slowly than every positive power of $n$. The supplementary archive contains the executable verifiers, exact certificates and archived verification records.

papers.title: Admissible geometries for Talenti's P\'olya--Szeg\H{o} principle
papers.abstract: Talenti symmetrization rearranges functions on an open connected set $X\subset\mathbb{R}^N$, endowed with a measure $\mu$ with continuous positive density, along the superlevel sets of a given function $f$. Talenti proved a P\'olya--Szeg\H{o} principle for it, provided that these sets are $\mu$-isoperimetric, have connected boundaries, and are crossed by straight lines of steepest ascent. We show that, if $X$ is convex, these requirements are very rigid: they force the superlevel sets of $f$ to be either parallel half-spaces, or concentric balls, or complements of tubes around an affine subspace of codimension at least two. This identifies the only geometries in which Talenti's P\'olya--Szeg\H{o} principle can be applied. We also prove a family of weighted isoperimetric inequalities in convex cones, showing that complements of tubes around affine subspaces of every codimension at least two do occur.

papers.title: Dimension reduction by bi-H\"older maps
papers.abstract: The H\"older dimension of a metric space is the infimum of its Hausdorff dimension over all bi-H\"older changes of the metric. Colvin asked whether it can take noninteger values. We show that every metric space of finite upper box dimension has integer H\"older dimension. For a bounded subset of a Euclidean space, the dimension reduction is carried out by a global homeomorphism of the ambient space, built from randomly translated singular functions, which brings the Hausdorff dimension of the set arbitrarily close to its integer part.

papers.title: Bounded Spaces without a Geodesic in the Gromov-Hausdorff Class
papers.abstract: We construct two countable complete bounded metric spaces at Gromov-Hausdorff distance $1/4$ with no midpoint and hence no shortest curve between them. The proof uses the local existence of optimal correspondences near a space with finitely many self-correspondences of distortion below a fixed positive threshold, each of which is the graph of a bijection.

papers.title: No regular icosahedron has a rational point on every face: a proof checked in Lean
papers.abstract: We prove that no regular icosahedron in $\mathbb{R}^3$ has a point with rational coordinates on each of its twenty closed faces, in every position, size and orientation, reflections included. This answers a question of I. Bogdanov on MathOverflow. A field automorphism of $\mathbb{C}$ that sends $\sqrt5$ to $-\sqrt5$ reduces the problem to the following statement: for every complex orthogonal $3\times3$ matrix $T$ some real linear combination of $\mathrm{Re}\,T$ and $\mathrm{Im}\,T$ separates ten intervals determined by the faces. We prove this statement by a computer-assisted case analysis over rational parametrizations of rotation frames, in which every inequality is an exact polynomial bound over $\mathbb{Z}[\varphi]$, $\varphi=(1+\sqrt5)/2$; no floating-point arithmetic and no Lipschitz estimates are used. The whole argument, including the $48$ certificates, is formalized in the Lean 4 proof assistant with Mathlib and checked by the Lean kernel; the main theorem depends only on the standard axioms. The mathematical argument and the formalization were produced by AI systems (OpenAI Codex and Anthropic Claude) under the direction of the author; see the statement at the end of the paper.

papers.title: The sharp bound on the distance between the centers of mass of a convex body and its boundary
papers.abstract: We prove that the distance between the centers of mass $c(K)$ and $c(\partial K)$ of a convex body $K$ and its boundary $\partial K$, respectively, does not exceed $ D_n$ times the width of $K$ in the direction of the vector joining $c(\partial K)$ and $c(K)$. The constant $D_n$ is optimal and coincides with the sharp constant in the problem of bounding the distance between the orthogonal projection of the centroid of a convex body onto a hyperplane and the centroid of its orthogonal projection onto that hyperplane.

papers.title: Discrete Coplanarity Rigidity and Local Mahler Volume Growth Near the Cube
papers.abstract: We study the finite-dimensional isovertex radial stratum of the cube, P(c)=conv{(1+c_q)q : q in Q_n={+/-1}^n}, with c(-q)=c(q), and establish quantitative rigidity and volume-product estimates for n>=3. The first main result identifies the kernel of the linearized facet-coplanarity operator R_n with the homothety direction span{1} and proves that the coplanarity defect is locally equivalent to both the transverse amplitude dist_infty(c,span{1}) and the distance d_GL(P(c),C_n) to the GL(n)-orbit of the cube. After normalizing out the homothety mode onto 1^perp, a key step is a second-order comparison between the linearized vertex-displacement seminorm and its optimization over small linear transformations. The second main result converts transverse radial perturbations c in 1^perp into a linear volume increment. A facetwise concave-envelope construction and an associated pocket functional yield the explicit primal lower bound vol(P(c))-2^n >= 8/(3(n-1))||c||_infty - O(||c||_infty^2) on 1^perp. Combining this with a chamber-independent first-order expansion of the polar volume (whose linear part vanishes on 1^perp with a uniform quadratic remainder) gives a linear lower bound for the Mahler product V_M(P(c))-V_M(C_n) in terms of d_GL(P(c),C_n). In dimension three, an exact chamber analysis on 1^perp yields vol(P(c))=8+(8/3)||c||_infty+O(||c||_infty^2), and the Mahler product has one-sided directional derivative (32/9)||u||_infty along every nonzero ray in 1^perp. In dimension four, a symmetry-orbit classification of the seventy balanced Boolean directions yields six combinatorial types and explicit first-order pocket bounds. We also distinguish the frozen-combinatorics KKT balance from geometric stationarity.

papers.title: Tiling an Equilateral Triangle
papers.abstract: Let $ABC$ be an equilateral triangle. For certain triangles $T$ (the ``tile'') and certain $N$, it is possible to cut $ABC$ into $N$ copies of $T$. It is known that only certain shapes of $T$ are possible, but until now very little was known about the possible values of $N$. Here we prove that for $N>3$, $N$ cannot be prime, and study more closely the possible tilings when the tile has a $\pi/3$ angle. All theorems have been formalized in Lean.

papers.title: Non-collapsed RCD spaces with local bounded covering geometry
papers.abstract: We study non-collapsed $\mathrm{RCD}(-(N-1),N)$ spaces with locally bounded covering geometry. Our first main result generalizes Gromov's almost flat manifold theorem: if the universal cover is non-collapsing and the diameter is sufficiently small, then the space is bi-Holder homeomorphic to an infranilmanifold. In the smooth setting with $\mathrm{Ric} \ge -(N-1)$, this homeomorphism is actually a diffeomorphism. As an application of our arguments, we show that Gromov's almost flat manifold theorem extends to the $\mathrm{RCD}+\mathrm{CBA}$ setting. Our second main result generalizes Fukaya's fibration theorem. Suppose a sequence of non-collapsed $\mathrm{RCD}(-(N-1),N)$ spaces with locally bounded covering geometry converges in the pointed measured Gromov--Hausdorff sense to a smooth manifold of dimension $k < N$. We then construct a topological fiber bundle map from the RCD spaces to the limit manifold. The fibers are infranilmanifolds, and the structure group is affine. Finally, although there exist collapsing Ricci limit spaces with no topological manifold points, we prove that if the sequence additionally satisfies locally bounded covering geometry and the limit space has dimension $k$, then every $k$-regular point is a topological manifold point.

papers.title: Timelike conjugate points in Lorentzian length spaces
papers.abstract: We study notions of conjugate points along timelike geodesics in the synthetic setting of Lorentzian (pre-)length spaces, inspired by earlier work for metric spaces by Shankar--Sormani. After preliminary considerations on convergence of timelike and causal geodesics, we introduce and compare one-sided, symmetric, unreachable and ultimate conjugate points along timelike geodesics. We show that all such notions are compatible with the usual one in the smooth (strongly causal) spacetime setting. As applications, we prove a timelike Rauch comparison theorem, as well as a result closely related to the recently established Lorentzian Cartan--Hadamard theorem by Er\"{o}s--Gieger. In the appendix, we give a detailed treatment of the Fr\'{e}chet distance on the space of non-stopping curves up to reparametrization, a technical tool used throughout the paper.

papers.title: Magnitude homology of real hyperplane arrangements
papers.abstract: We define and study the magnitude and magnitude homology of real hyperplane arrangements by regarding their tope graphs as metric spaces. Since magnitude is a refinement of the cardinality, this may be viewed as a natural generalization of the classical problem of counting the chambers of an arrangement. Our central result is a structure theorem asserting that the magnitude and magnitude homology of an arrangement decompose into contributions indexed by its faces. In particular, the magnitude is determined by the intersection lattice of the arrangement. We also observe several interesting phenomena, including a characterization of Boolean arrangements in terms of diagonality and a reciprocity theorem reminiscent of Ehrhart--Macdonald reciprocity. Finally, based on explicit computations, we conjecture that the magnitude homology of an arrangement is torsion-free and determined by its intersection lattice.

papers.title: Triangle Tiling: The case $3\alpha + 2\beta = \pi$
papers.abstract: An $N$-tiling of triangle $ABC$ by triangle $T$ (the ``tile'') is a way of writing $ABC$ as a union of $N$ copies of $T$ overlapping only at their boundaries. Let the tile $T$ have angles $(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$, and sides $(a,b,c)$. This paper takes up the case when $3\alpha + 2\beta = \pi$. Then there are (as was already known) exactly five possible shapes of $ABC$ not similar to $T$: either $ABC$ is isosceles with base angles $\alpha$, $\beta$, or $\alpha+\beta$, or the angles of $ABC$ are $(2\alpha,\beta,\alpha+\beta)$, or the angles of $ABC$ are $(2\alpha, \alpha, 2\beta)$. We prove that the tile is rational (the ratios of its sides are rational). We then exhibit several families of previously unknown tilings. We also exhibit, for each shape, a Diophantine equation in $N$ and the parameters of the tile that must have a solution whenever there is a tiling of some triangle of that shape. By means of these Diophantine equations, some conclusions about the possible values of $N$ are drawn. We prove, for example, that there is no $N$-tiling with $N$ prime when $3\alpha + 2\beta = \pi$, for three of the five shapes; that question remains open for the shape $(2\alpha,\beta,\alpha+\beta)$ and for isosceles triangles with base angles $\beta$. These equations also imply that for each $N$, there is a finite set of possibilities for the tile $(a,b,c)$ and the triangle $ABC$. (Usually, but not always, there is just one possible tile.) For each of the five shapes, we give a construction method that works under certain sufficient conditions, but there remain values of $N$ that satisfy our necessary conditions and for which we do not know whether a tiling exists. All results have been formalized in Lean.
